Let me explain it for others who might be trying to follow this. They are counting sealed court proceedings. There a tons of reasons documents filed with PACER might be sealed, indictments tend to only be a small part of what is marked as SEALED in PACER. Anytime you have a criminal case with a juvenile defendant that case is automatically sealed. All of the following are cases that would be sealed in Federal courts, Misdemeanor Drug Cases, Documents showing Cooperating witnesses, Transfers of Jurisdiction, any grand jury matters and any type of warrant. Sometimes cases are sealed to protect the victims, sometimes cases are sealed to protect Trade Secrets. There's a few other reasons too and this is just the criminal side, the civil side has a bunch too.

And sealed indictments are often unsealed very quickly. The documents in the NXVIM case show this pretty clearly, when the Mack and Raniere indictment got unsealed, the press release went out on Friday, April 20, 2018

Actor Allison Mack was arrested this morning on an indictment unsealed today in federal court in Brooklyn charging her and Keith Raniere

The indictment that was unsealed on April 20th? It was sealed at 4PM on the April 19th. Look at the seal on the document: link is below. It was literally sealed for less than a day. And this is the case with a lot of indictments. They are sealed for a short time, because of court time, grand jury schedules, finalizing paperwork, preparing arrests or press conferences, etc. Now indictments are returned by a grand jury after the prosecutor presents evidence. But in this case, the police applied for an arrest warrant in February. In fact, they asked for a sealed arrest warrant. This is done by an officer or agent presenting evidence directly to a judge and would allow the FBI to arrest Raniere before the indictments were finished, if they thought he was trying to leave the country. So if you were counting every "sealed" proceeding in this case as an indictment, you just double counted and this is not counting all the documents in this case, just the ones you can find on the DOJ website.
